gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Raw and rowdy, Disorder sets its glyphs well apart and lets curves meet stems without any swelling. Noto Sans Old Hungarian stays open and friendly right down to tiny sizes.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: No swelling where curves meet stems gives Disorder its raw, chaotic bite, with every glyph set well apart. Noto Sans Old Italic is the quiet counterweight, its capitals barely above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Loud and spread out, Disorder gives its diagonals full weight. Shouting is what the heading does best, while Noto Sans Old North Arabian is best at packing a dense, tall lowercase band.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Bent tubing, loose and loud: that is Disorder. Noto Sans Old Permic sits opposite, with rounded, open forms and lowercase nearly level with the capitals, a real tonal gap.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Chunky and loud: Disorder draws everything in one thick outline and sets its glyphs well apart. Noto Sans Oriya keeps its curve gaps generous and its small letters tall.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong reads contemporary and unfussy, with rounds that gap open like a cracked bangle and a high-set x-height. Disorder earns its keep big and short, free of calligraphic thinning.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-psalter: Disorder is all constant-ink stripes and wide-set glyphs, with a high x-height that makes its lowercase look big. Shrink it, and Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, gaping e and all, takes over.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads approachable, with a large central band. Next to it, Disorder feels flat and stencil-cut, each stroke a single weight, a rough cutout beside something soft.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Chaotic from the first glance, Disorder has no hairlines anywhere and sets its glyphs well apart. But Noto Sans Tamil Supplement does its best work with round forms like open parentheses.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Noto Sans Tangsa reads welcoming, with generous round openings and short ascender stems. Against it, Disorder draws a steady, pressureless line with glyphs flung apart, and that rough-versus-friendly gap is the appeal.
